jobs.title: Prevention Consultant at State of Vermont
jobs.description: Employer: State of Vermont Expires: 11/19/2026 The Local Health Division of the Health Department is a system of 12 Local Health Offices, providing a public health presence in every community in Vermont. Local Health works across a broad range of public health programmatic areas improving the social, environmental, and economic conditions that affect health and health equity. The Bennington District Office is seeking a Substance Misuse Prevention Consultant (PC). PCs play a critical role in Vermont's state-wide system to prevent substance misuse. Working in partnership with community coalitions, schools, faith-based organizations, local law enforcement, and others, PCs facilitate a process of assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of best practices for prevention programs. PCs also support and assist with the administration of the Division of Substance Use Programs (DSU) prevention grants to community organizations. Responsibilities include:Using public health data and engaging with partners to identify prevention-related needs, opportunities, and priorities.Strategically supporting the implementation of best practice strategies to address community priorities for prevention, and to promote protective factors.Providing regional outreach and education to partners working on substance misuse prevention and encouraging new partners to begin contributing to sustainable prevention strategies.Offering presentations on prevention-related topics to a variety of audiences, prioritizing presentations that meet DSU-grantee needs.Identifying and developing region-specific goals to address the needs and readiness of the local region and to support collaborative solutions.Promoting health equity by addressing root causes of difference in health outcomes as it relates to substance misuse. PCs work as part of a local team that promotes policy, community, and organizational level strategies to improve health outcomes. They also collaborate with 10 other PCs across the state, and with the state-level Division of Substance Use Programs. This position participates as part of a multidisciplinary public health team, including engaging in Health Department emergency preparedness efforts. DIVISION OF LOCAL HEATH - Who We Are The Division of Local Health works to preserve and improve the equitable social, economic, and environmental conditions necessary to attain the highest level of health and well-being for all, thus ensuring healthy Vermonters. The Division of Local Health is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming environment that respects and celebrates every person's strength, assets, and values. The Division of Local Health is committed to leading organizational change efforts that address avoidable inequities and injustices as we work towards the elimination of health and health care disparities. TELEWORK The Department of Health supports a hybrid work environment which combines both in person and remote work. Upon hire, employees work with their supervisor to create a schedule that aligns with the business needs of the unit and complies with State of Vermont policy. We believe a hybrid work environment promotes autonomy and allows for increased flexibility and greater work/life balance. MISSIONPromote the physical, mental, and social well-being of people in Vermont by advancing equity, protecting against disease and injury, and preparing for health emergencies.VISIONAll people and communities in Vermont have equitable opportunities to achieve their highest level of health and well-being.VALUESEquity: We aim to center health justice and address racism and all forms of oppression in our programs and policies, our approach to collaboration, and how we build and nurture our workforce.Collaboration: We engage with staff and partners to understand complex problems and design responsive solutions.Inclusion: We support a culture of belonging and diversity where people are valued, trusted, and able to be their authentic selves.Harmony: We endorse a balanced, thoughtful, and intentional work environment that allows employees to care for themselves, their families, and the people they serve.Data: We strive for scientific excellence and cultural responsiveness in the collection, analysis, sharing and use of data. Minimum Qualifications Three (3) years or more of experience in public health, human services, emergency response, community engagement, program administration, human services related fields or health-related fields. ORAssociate degree in public health, public administration, business administration, environmental science, emergency response, human services, social work, social sciences related fields or health-related fields and two (2) years or more of experience in public health, human services, emergency response, community engagement, program administration, human services related fields or health-related fields. ORBachelor’s degree in public health, public administration, business administration, environmental science, emergency response, human services, social sciences related fields or health-related fields and one (1) year or more of experience in public health, human services, emergency response, community engagement, program administration, human services related fields or health-related fields. ORMaster’s degree in public health, public administration, business administration, environmental science, emergency response, human services, social sciences related fields or health-related fields.OROne (1) year or more of experience as Public Health Specialist I.

jobs.title: Victory Congressional Internship at LGBTQ Victory Institute
jobs.description: Employer: LGBTQ Victory Institute Expires: 11/19/2026 Are you a passionate and driven undergraduate student looking to make a real impact in the world? LGBTQ+ Victory Institute's Victory Congressional Internship, designed for LGBTQ+ students, is offering a life-changing opportunity for outstanding students like you. Join us for an 8-week internship on Capitol Hill, along with weekly leadership development activities in the heart of Washington, DC.About the Internship:The Victory Congressional Internship aims to develop the next generation of LGBTQ+ public leaders by providing hands-on experience and valuable insights into the federal legislative process. You will have the chance to intern with a member of the Congressional Equality Caucus or an LGBTQ-friendly member of the U.S. Congress, learning firsthand how policy decisions are made at the highest level.Empowering LGBTQ+ Leaders:We are committed to nurturing informed decision-makers and influential leaders who can bring about positive change in their communities and beyond. To ensure you can fully focus on your growth and development, we provide a stipend, cover transportation to and from D.C, and pay for your travel within the city. Financial concerns should not stand in the way of your aspirations – LGBTQ+ Victory Institute provides housing at no cost to you.A Comprehensive Leadership Program:Our internship program is not just about the internship itself. It includes a weekly educational and leadership development program that spans various policy-making careers. Engage with subject-matter experts from diverse working sectors across the District of Columbia, exploring topics such as personal leadership, LGBTQ+ history and advocacy, community engagement and service, and public policy.International LGBTQ Leaders Conference:In December 2027, you will have the unique opportunity to attend LGBTQ+ Victory Institute’s annual International LGBTQ+ Leaders Conference. Join hundreds of out LGBTQ+ leaders in government, politics, advocacy, business, and community organizations for three days of training, skills-building, networking, and engaging discussions.Program Dates and Expectations:The summer program will begin with move-in on Wednesday, May 26, 2027, and will run through move-out on Sunday, July 25, 2027. As a committed intern, you are expected to be available to work during traditional business hours, approximately 40 hours per week.Apply Now:Take the first step towards becoming an influential leader by applying through LGBTQ+ Victory Institute's website. Click the "Apply Externally" button to start your journey with us. We will not review applications only submitted through Handshake. Contact Information:For any questions, feel free to reach out to Sarah Pope (she/they), Senior Director of Leadership Development Programs at sarah[dot]pope@victoryinstitute[dot]org. Join us in making a difference and driving positive change for the LGBTQ+ community and beyond!

jobs.title: EPA Data Science Fellowship for the Endocrine Disruption Screening Program at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/20/2026 Description*Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.EPA Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP), within the Endocrine Disruptor Screening Program (EDSP), located in Durham, North Carolina. You will receive training in the Research Triangle Park, NC campus and may be required to travel to Washington, DC once a year for debriefings.The mission of EPA is to protect human health and the environment. EPA works to ensure that: Americans have clean air, land and water; National efforts to reduce environmental risks are based on the best available scientific information; Federal laws protecting human health and the environment are administered and enforced fairly, effectively and as Congress intended; Environmental stewardship is integral to U.S. policies concerning natural resources, human health, economic growth, energy, transportation, agriculture, industry, and international trade, and these factors are similarly considered in establishing environmental policy; All parts of society have access to accurate information sufficient to effectively participate in managing human health and environmental risks; Contaminated lands and toxic sites are cleaned up; and chemicals in the marketplace are reviewed for safety.Research Project: You will gain experience in data management, analysis, and technical skills for coordinated research and informatics efforts supporting EDSP. The appointment will focus on data science activities related to toxicological and targeted bioactivity screening data as part of the US EPA Toxicity Forecaster (ToxCast) program, including model maintenance, productionizing research endpoints, development of R packages, software development, database curation, and quality evaluation of in vitro chemical screening data. Research activities may include acquiring domain knowledge in toxicology and chemistry; wrangling heterogeneous source formats into standard templates; conducting data analysis and curation using controlled vocabularies; performing database scripting; managing code libraries and documentation; identifying and correcting bugs; conducting user acceptance testing; developing automated tools for processing large volumes of data; and applying innovative data science solutions to support hazard identification, screening prioritization, risk assessment, and regulatory decision-making. You may also gain experience with the evaluations of the predictivity and precision of new approach methods (NAMs) relative to traditional animal testing.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will learn how to: Design and implement reusable and scalable techniques for data managementOrganize or transform data in databases to support scientific analyses Analyze data quality according to specified criteriaWrite scripts and functions in R to support data migration and data curation software toolsDevelop and collaborate with others to evolve scientific applications into production level toolsCreate and interact with RESTful APIs to support scientific effortsCreate proof of concept projects and adapting/maintaining code from other researchersOther research activities may include:Gain experience being a part of an interdisciplinary team of software developers, data scientists, and subject-matter experts.Develop skills in creating clear, effective data visualizations to communicate results to stakeholders and technical audiences.Build proficiency in thoroughly documenting data, code, analytical methods, and procedures in accordance with EPA quality-assurance procedures, supporting transparency and reproducibility.Strengthen technical writing skills by drafting reports that describe complex datasets, data-processing methods, and data-manipulation procedures.Prepare internal reports and memoranda that communicate analytical research and findings for use by EPA scientists.Develop scientific communication experience through opportunities to present research at scientific conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed manuscripts.Mentor(s): The mentors for this opportunity are Madison Feshuk (feshuk.madison@epa.gov) and Scott Lynn (lynn.scott@epa.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: December 1, 2026. All start dates are flexible and vary depending on numerous factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year and may be renewed three to four additional years upon EPA recommendation and subject to availability of funding.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.EPA Security Clearance: Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at EPA.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and EPA. Participants do not become employees of EPA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.ORISE offers all ORISE EPA graduate students and Postdocs a free 5 year membership to the National Postdoctoral Association (NPA).The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility.Questions: Please see the FAQ section of our website. If you have additional questions about the application process please email ORISE.EPA.OCSPP@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received a bachelor's or master's degree in one of the relevant fields (toxicology, environmental science, cell/molecular biology, biochemistry, or a closely related field of study). Degree must have been received within the past five years.Preferred skills:Training or courses in statistics or computer programmingDomain knowledge of biology or toxicology processes desiredStrong reading comprehension skills and experience logically interpreting pieces of information from a variety of data source typesExperience programming in the R languageExperience utilizing R packages for code development and data analysis, such as devtools and tidyverse, desiredExperience writing CRAN compliant R packages and/or functions desiredExperience with relational databases, such as MySQL, PostGreSQL, or others Stipend$52,693.00 – $64,453.00 YearlyPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsCitizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree received within the last 60 month(s).

jobs.description: Employer: Nebraska Department of Health & Human Services Expires: 11/20/2026 Our Child and Family Services Internship will learn how our Child and Family Services Specialist serve some of our most vulnerable populations. If you are currently enrolled in a college or university, and require an internship to complete course work, take a look at this opportunity! We have opportunities at many of our local DHHS offices across the State.Onsite Locations Include: Omaha, Lincoln, Scottsbluff, Chadron, Nebraska City, Norfolk, South Sioux City, Hastings, Grand Island, Kearney, York, Seward, Fremont, Ogallala, and More. Application Review: March 1st, 2027 Application Deadline: March 26th, 2027 Interns will shadow our Child and Family Service Specialist to gain hands on experience. CFSS roles are rewarding, yet challenging, as they provide opportunities, services, and programs that promote a healthy, safe, and stable environment for children/youth in our communities with their caregivers. CFSS work closely with families that need child welfare intervention because of abuse and/or neglect. CFSS will sometimes work with the legal system toward permanency goals. Case managers are trained on resources necessary to help children and families heal from trauma in their lives, and on the importance of promoting community safety. In Children & Family Services, we aim to provide the least disruptive services when needed, for only the amount of time necessary to give children the opportunity to succeed, live with dignity and respect and help families care for themselves. This will result in healthier families and safer, more prosperous communities. jobs.description: Employer: Rocky Mountain Conservancy Expires: 11/20/2026 Rocky Mountain Conservancy is excited to offer two seasonal environmental education fellowships that give current students and recent college graduates the opportunity to serve in a national park while exploring careers in environmental education and the nonprofit sector. Each fellowship includes: On-the-job training and experience in a variety of environmental education programs and settings Opportunities to develop and lead programs individually and in partnership with both Rocky Mountain Conservancy (RMC) and Rocky Mountain National Park (RMNP) teams Housing and utilities are provided at no cost along with a stipend for living expenses Professional development and networking opportunities with park and nonprofit staff As a fellow, you will have the opportunity to build real-world experience in both the nonprofit and public sectors. Our fellowship will help you develop: A deep understanding of the Conservancy’s work and partnerships Knowledge of the region’s natural and cultural history Skills in program planning and delivery, participant communication, and outreach A professional portfolio of education and outreach work products Required Skills: Dedication to environmental and outdoor education, with the ability to lead programs for children, teens, and adults Adept communication skills, both written and spoken, for diverse audiences and using various media Strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to organize ideas and information quickly Demonstrated ability to independently manage long-term projects and complete assignments on time Desire and ability to work both collaboratively and independently Computer experience with Canva and the Microsoft Office suite, including Word and Outlook, preferred Enthusiasm, a warm disposition, and the ability to handle the stresses of working outdoors with diverse groups of program participants Responsibilities: Develop and lead interactive outdoor programs (i.e. pop-up table talks, and educational bus tours) for diverse audiences, including families, youth, and adults Support expert-led Field Institute programsAssist with development, planning, and implementation for a range of Conservancy programs Support RMNP education and interpretation programs, such as school field trips and Jr. Ranger programs Create outreach and promotional materials for Conservancy programs Establish and maintain positive working relationships with RMNP staff and volunteers, as well as with other Conservancy partners, program participants, and community members Assist Conservancy and park staff with outreach events Drive and/or ride in Conservancy-owned vehicles, including the Conservancy’s 15-passenger buses Each position averages 30-40 hours per week, with schedules that vary throughout the fellowship. jobs.description: Employer: Appalachian Conservation Corps Expires: 11/22/2026 Title: Invasive Plant Management Individual PlacementPositions: 5 positions availableLocation: Based out of Washington, DCDates of Service: February 17th, 2026 - November 19th, 2027 (40 weeks)Schedule: Monday – Thursday, 630 am to 5pm, 10 hours/dayPay: $800/week ($600/stipend + $200/additional benefit) paid biweeklyStatus: This is a full-time, temporary 1200-hour AmeriCorps National Service position.Questions? Contact ACCIPrecruiting@conservationlegacy.org Applications will be accepted on our website through November 22nd. Please submit a resume and cover letter with your application. Appalachian Conservation Corps: Our Individual Placement program works to connect young people to conservation service across Appalachia and neighboring communities in Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, DC, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. ACC is a program of Conservation Legacy, a nationwide network of conservation organizations. When joining this AmeriCorps program, participants commit to a term of service at their placement site and in return gain hands-on experience and a variety of benefits to help them succeed in achieving their career goals. ACC welcomes national applicants, but also emphasizes the engagement of local individuals who represent the communities in which they serve. Position Summary:The Invasive Plant Management Individual Placement is based in Washington, D.C., working directly with the National Capital Region of the National Park Service. This 10-month AmeriCorps position will serve as a member of the Invasive Plant Management Team (IPMT). This hands-on opportunity allows youth partners to help protect national parks across the region while building valuable skills in conservation and natural resource management. As a member of the IPMT, youth partner will learn how to identify and manage invasive plants species using mechanical and chemical control methods. Training and field work will include herbicide applications using backpack sprayers and gas operated tank sprayers, chainsaws, brush cutters, hand saws, loppers and more!While this position primarily involves fieldwork, the youth partner may also contribute to office projects, including reviewing scientific literature to identify the most effective control methods for newly detected invasive species, creating internal science briefs on rare vegetation found in parks supported by IPMT, and assisting with the development of other communication materials. Beyond invasive plant management, IPs will have opportunities to learn from NPS staff about other aspects of natural resource management, attend NPS-sponsored training, and participate in activities with other resource programs to broaden their knowledge and experience. During their terms, members will receive training and certifications to be able to identify and treat a variety of invasive plant species. This position is heavily field based and involves frequent travel to parks in the capital region and daily physical activity. Housing is NOT provided for this position. We are seeking candidates who are current residents of Washington, D.C. or surrounding metro area. Benefits: $800/week living stipend, paid bi-weekly $5,176.50 AmeriCorps Segal Education Award upon successful completion of 1200 hour service term (award amount varies based on length of commitment and can be used for paying off federal student loans or paying tuition for a Title IV accredited college) $120 reimbursement for work boots with receipt, $100 for local ID guidesOption to enroll in health, vision and dental insuranceEligibility for the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority upon successful completion – noncompetitive hiring status for two years when applying for federal positions.Federal student loan forbearance and interest payoffMember Assistance Program– 3 free sessions of support with a counseling or work-life balance specialist Additional subject-specific certifications and trainings may be offered (Chainsaw training, pesticides, etc)Depending upon the academic institution and program, positions may fulfill internship requirements Professional development opportunities (mentorship, resume support, alumni listserv, etc.) and exposure to natural resource career paths General Qualifications:To qualify for this AmeriCorps position, you must be between the ages of 21 and 30, (or 35 if a veteran) and a US citizen that has received a high school diploma or GED. All offers of employment are conditional upon completion of an acceptable check of the National Sex Offender Public Registry and federal criminal background check. Must be eligible to receive an AmeriCorps Education Award.Possess a valid driver’s license.Physically capable of strenuous field activities (hiking, monitoring, survey, testing, etc) for 10 hours in adverse conditions (high heat, high humidity, biting insects, rough terrain, inclement weather)Comfortable working in a field and office environmentMust be able to lift 50 lbs. Preferred Qualifications:Two or four year college degree in a biology-related subject area or related experienceFamiliarity with local plant identificationA minimum of 3 years of driving experienceDemonstrated experience in a field environment How to Apply:Please submit a resume that highlights any education, work or volunteer experience, skills and trainings that may apply to this position. Applications are only accepted through our website, www.appalachiancc.org/individualplacements. jobs.title: Public Policy & Advocacy Internship – Spring 2027 at U.S. Chamber of Commerce
jobs.description: Employer: U.S. Chamber of Commerce Expires: 11/23/2026 We are pleased to offer an outstanding and substantive internship program for the nation's best and brightest young leaders.At the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, you will obtain a hands-on, meaningful work experience designed to meet your academic and career goals. Our internships offer opportunities in research, writing, database management, policy, communications, and event preparation.During the internship, you will network with colleagues and senior executives while participating in educational and professional activities designed to enhance your experience. PROGRAM OVERVIEW:The Chamber Internship Program is a one-of-a-kind opportunity to learn at the world's largest business organization. In addition to directly supporting a team in the organization, interns have an opportunity to participate in a variety of programming that will help build professional skills and networks.Responsibilities for interns typically include research, drafting memos, content creation, and event planning and coordination. Specific responsibilities vary by department and semester.The Chamber also offers robust programming each semester to support professional development and networking for interns. These opportunities include company-wide meetings and social events, intern-exclusive discussions with senior executives such as the CEO, the Chief Policy Officer, and the President of the Foundation, as well as a resume review and interview preparation workshop.The internship is expected to run from February 1 through April 9. Interns work a part-time hybrid schedule and are expected to be in the office at least three days a week at our U.S. Chamber of Commerce headquarters in downtown Washington, D.C. Fully remote applicants will not be considered. Interns will be responsible for making their own housing accommodations if needed.This is a paid internship, and students may also receive academic credit if they meet the criteria set by their school. The hourly rate for this position is between $18.00 and $20.00 per hour. This internship is open to current college or graduate students, as well as individuals who have graduated within the past six months. DEPARTMENT MATCHINGThe Public Policy & Advocacy teams shape U.S. and global policy on critical issues including economic growth, energy, cybersecurity, employment, healthcare, and strategic advocacy. Interns will support policy research, legislative tracking, stakeholder engagement, and communications efforts that advance the Chamber’s pro-business priorities across public and private sectors.After you submit your resume, our Talent Acquisition team will review it. If your skills match what we are looking for, the relevant department will reach out for an interview.Please review the departments below closely. In the application, please indicate your top two department preferences. Cyber, Space, & National Security PolicyThe National Security Policy division advocates on behalf of the Chamber's members who have a direct stake in cybersecurity, defense, space, and supply chain security policy. Interns support the team with preparation, research, and materials for major events including the March Aerospace event and roundtables across cyber, space, and defense, as well as international trip preparation. This role is ideal for candidates with an interest in national security, technology policy, and Capitol Hill engagement. Economic PolicyThe U.S. Chamber's Economic Policy team serves as an in-house quantitative resource for member companies, state and local chambers, and policy teams across the building. Interns play a hands-on role tracking economic data releases and trends to support outlook briefings, assisting as quantitative consultants on domestic and international policy work, and exploring new applications of AI in the team's day-to-day operations. This is a great fit for candidates with a strong interest in economics, data analysis, and applied policy research. Employment PolicyThe Employment Policy team advances the Chamber's workforce, education, and labor policy priorities on behalf of American businesses. Interns take on substantive ownership across three core areas: supporting planning and execution of the Child Care Fly-In (a key grant deliverable), revamping the America Works homepage to strengthen external communications on education and workforce issues, and helping prepare members for ILO negotiations on chemical hazards and AI in the workplace. This role is ideal for candidates interested in labor policy, workforce development, and international employer advocacy. Global Energy InstituteThe U.S. Chamber's Global Energy Institute unifies energy stakeholders and policymakers behind a common strategy to ensure America's supply of fuel and power is adequate, stable, and affordable, while protecting national security and improving the environment. Interns support the team across three core areas: event logistics and stakeholder engagement for high-profile convenings, policy research across the electric generation, permitting, and international energy portfolios, and strategic communications including one-pagers, blog posts, newsletters, and briefing materials. A great fit for candidates interested in energy policy, advocacy, and the intersection of policy and communications. Government AffairsThe Government Affairs division is the Chamber's lobbying team, headquartered in Washington with regional offices across the country, championing pro-business priorities and advocating for America's free enterprise system on Capitol Hill. Interns support the team with congressional hearing preparation, drafting member briefing profiles, organizing testimony materials, tracking legislation, and supporting policy forums and Hill activities. Interns are also encouraged to attend Hill meetings and events, gaining firsthand exposure to the legislative process and the Chamber's advocacy work. Housing PolicyThe Housing Policy team leads the Chamber’s national initiative to address America’s housing shortage by advancing pro-growth policies that increase housing supply and affordability. Interns support the team across three core areas: land use and permitting reform, housing finance and capital access, and workforce and immigration policy. Responsibilities include policy research, legislative tracking, stakeholder engagement, and communications support to advance the Chamber’s housing advocacy efforts. This role is ideal for candidates interested in housing policy, economic growth, and public policy development. Chamber Technology Engagement CenterThe Chamber Technology Engagement Center (C_TEC) is at the forefront of the Chamber's work on emerging technology policy, including artificial intelligence, robotics, and quantum computing. Interns play a direct role in drafting white papers on these cutting-edge topics and tracking technology legislation across states — work that directly shapes the Chamber's policy positions and thought leadership. This is an ideal opportunity for candidates passionate about technology policy, innovation, and the future of the digital economy. Applications are accepted until Thursday, October 12. Interviews will be conducted in November & December.This internship requires U.S. work authorization and is open to candidates with Curricular Practical Training (CPT) and/or Optional Practical Training (OPT).We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: USDA-FS Fellowship for Preparation and Analysis of Environmental Samples for Forest Productivity Studies at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/26/2026 Application Deadline10/30/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.USDA Forest Service Office/Lab and Location: A fellowship opportunity is available with the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service (FS) within the Forest Service Northern Research Station (NRS) located in Grand Rapids, Minnisota.At the heart of the USDA Forest Service's mission is their purpose. Everything they do is intended to help sustain forests and grasslands for present and future generations. Why? Because their stewardship work supports nature in sustaining life. This is the purpose that drives the agency’s mission and motivates their work across the agency. It’s been there from the agency’s very beginning, and it still drives them. To advance the mission and serve their purpose, the USDA Forest Service balances the short and long-term needs of people and nature by: working in collaboration with communities and our partners; providing access to resources and experiences that promote economic, ecological, and social vitality; connecting people to the land and one another; and delivering world-class science, technology and land management.Research Project: You will focus soil and forest floor samples and their preparation for long-term, forest-productivity studies. You will experience how to collect and analyze vegetation data. Mentored by a research scientist, you will train on laboratory techniques and equipment used by a laboratory manager (chemist), a physical sciences technician, forest ecologist, and other staff. Through these interactions, you will see how and why samples are prepared for chemical analysis, and how analysis of soil and vegetation data contributes to forest ecology studies. jobs.title: Foster Youth Internship Program® at Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute Expires: 11/28/2026 Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute’s (CCAI) Foster Youth Internship (FYI) Program® is a competitive national internship for students and recent graduates with lived experience in the US foster care system who are interested in federal policy and advocacy. Participants write a federal child welfare policy report and are placed in the Washington, D.C. legislative offices of Members of the U.S. Congress. Participants will travel to D.C. for the 8 week program over the summer and will be required to live in dormitory-style housing provided by CCAI. The Foster Youth Internship Program® closes to applicants on November 15th, 2026.The Foster Youth Internship Program® (FYI) began in 2003 as an effort to raise awareness to federal policymakers about the needs and unique perspectives of individuals who have experienced the U.S. foster care system. CCAI works with congressional offices to secure a congressional internship for each participant. In addition, CCAI organizes an orientation, advocacy trainings, networking, and various other professional development opportunities. These combined experiences allow the participants to create a policy report that is presented to U.S. Congress, Administration, Department of Health and Human Services, and released to policymakers and advocates across the country. As a result of the program, federal policymakers learn firsthand the experiences of youth in foster care and go on to use their new knowledge to inspire legislative change to federal child welfare policy. Participants benefit both personally and professionally, gaining experience and skills that will bolster their careers for years to come. This is an immersive eight-week, educational, and civic experience in Washington, D.C. with a comprehensive onboarding to ensure participants are well-prepared for effective advocacy and leadership development in the nation's capital. Participants are not considered employees of CCAI nor their congressional office. CCAI provides a monthly stipend during the remote preparatory onboarding (February 1 - May 28) and weekly stipend while in Washington, D.C. (May 31 - July 23), and covers major expenses, such as housing in Washington, D.C., transportation to/from Washington, D.C., and public transportation to/from the congressional office internship. Participants are responsible for some smaller expenses. Interns are required to live in dormitory-style housing assigned by CCAI for the duration of the program and to adhere to the guidance and regulations of the program.Each congressional office placement differs. CCAI does not guarantee that the intern will be assigned projects that are related to child welfare. Office responsibilities will likely include: Open, sort, and deliver mailAnswer phones, greet constituents, run errands, deliver priority letters, and acquire signaturesCopy, file, fax, data entry, and work on small legislative projects Work directly with congressional staff to research issues and compose constituent correspondenceAttend committee hearings, sit in on meetings, attend press conferences, and take notes Provide constituent services and give tours of the U.S. Capitol Attend and assist with congressional briefings and meetings, including various events organized by CCAI The Foster Youth Internship Program® closes to applicants on November 15th, 2026.Please review our eligibility requirements, due dates, and all other necessary info at https://www.ccainstitute.org/programs/view/foster-youth-internship-apply to learn more or join us for our last info session on October 23rd! If you have questions after carefully reviewing this application and the information available on CCAI’ s website about the Foster Youth Internship Program®, please contact Lisette DuFore Benz at lisette@cccainstitute.org or (202) 544-8500 ext. 12.

jobs.title: Environmental Steward Crew Leader at Polk County Conservation
jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 11/28/2026 Polk County Conservation envisions a transformative process of utilizing AmeriCorps volunteers to manage undermanaged natural ecosystems in Iowa. The Environmental Steward Crew Leader plays a vital role in the management and stewardship of natural resources within Polk County Conservation’s parks and green spaces. Working under the direction of the Natural Resources full-time staff, the Crew Leader participates in a wide range of natural resource projects aimed at enhancing and maintaining the ecological health and biodiversity of county-owned lands.The Three-Quarter Time Environmental Steward Crew Leader will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($16,620) paid equally over the course of 1200 hours from the start to the end of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon completion ($5,176.50) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. These positions are three-quarter time volunteers who will serve a minimum of 1200 hours over 39 weeks, serving 38 hours per week.This posting is not a direct position of Polk County Conservation, and successful applicants will not be employees of Polk County. Successful applicants will not be subject to terms and conditions of Polk County employment and will not be eligible for any employee benefits provided by Polk County. However, these positions will be serving with Polk County Conservation, a host site of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program, and will be subject to AmeriCorps rules, benefits, and federal requirements. Daily TimesThe typical weekly schedule will run from 6:30am to 4:30pm on a Monday through Thursday schedule, totaling to 38 hours per weekEvery service day will include two 15-minute breaks; additional breaks must be taken if the temperature is above 85 degreesA 30-minute lunch period is included with every service day; these 30 minutes cannot be counted towards the required service hours during the termThe typical weekly schedule may change to better meet the needs of the Natural Resources Department* Volunteers must not serve any hours on the major federal holidays – New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. This includes checking emails, self-directed training, or teleservice. If the Host Site is open on one of these holidays and volunteers are expected to serve, the site supervisor should work with Program to gain approval for this volunteer service prior to the holiday. For any of the other federal holidays, including MLK Day, Presidents Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans Day, Host Sites will communicate expectations of volunteer service in advance. If the Host Site is closed on one of more of those lesser holidays (including the day after Thanksgiving or Christmas eve) or the Host Site recognizes other workdays when major federal holidays fall on weekend days, volunteers should not check their email, complete timesheets, or do teleservice on those days either unless they follow the procedure above. Sick or personal leave, and holidays is allowed, but such time off does not count towards the required number of hours needed to successfully complete the term of service. There are additional benefits offered if the volunteer has a compelling personal circumstance. TrainingAll volunteers will go through two weeks of intensive in-person training to learn all the skills necessary to complete the volunteer duties outlined below.The Environmental Steward Crew Leader AmeriCorps Volunteer will lead and actively participate in a variety of natural resources management and conservation activities. The focus of the position is hands-on service, fostering environmental stewardship, and contributing to the overall improvement and preservation of natural habitats. The Crew Leader will be responsible for leading a team of AmeriCorps volunteers in executing impactful projects such as invasive species removal, timber stand improvement, prairie seed harvest, prairie burning, trail maintenance, and pollinator garden planting.Volunteers will receive the following training and certifications before service activities begin:Volunteers will complete CPR/AED and first aid certification through Heart Saver online modules and an in-person practical skills testMental Health First Aid trainingVolunteers will participate in a week-long chainsaw handling and maintenance training and pass a in-person practical skills test with full-time Polk County Conservation natural resources staff volunteersIowa Pesticide Applicator Certification in Categories 4 (Core), 2 (Forestry) and 6 (Right of Way)Volunteers must read each designated booklet in order to register for each corresponding category testTesting occurs online and utilizes LockDown Browser application that records video of the tester during the timed tests; personal laptops may be utilized for testing or computers will be available for volunteers to useVolunteers must receive an 80% or better to receive category certificationsVolunteers receive their Iowa Pesticide Applicator’s License once all three category tests are successfully passedNational Wildland Coordinating Group Certifications:S-130 – Firefighter TrainingS-190 – Introduction to Wildland Fire BehaviorThey may also have the opportunity to receive additional certifications in:L-180 – Human Factors in the Wildland Fire ServiceIS-700 – NIMS (National Incident Management System): An IntroductionAll AmeriCorps Environmental Stewards in the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program are required to complete CPR/AED and first aid online modules; Mental Health First Aid training; Iowa Pesticide Applicator tests in Core, 2, and 6; and the National Wildland Coordinating Group online modules of S-130 and S-190 within three weeks subsequent to their official start date. Failure to complete these trainings and certifications in a timely manner will result in a volunteer not receiving integral certifications utilized by the Program. Missing or skipping trainings and certifications could impact the ability of a volunteer to remain enrolled within the Program. jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 11/28/2026 Polk County Conservation envisions a transformative process of utilizing AmeriCorps volunteers to manage under-managed natural ecosystems in Iowa. The Environmental Steward Crew Member plays a vital role in the management and stewardship of natural resources within Polk County Conservation’s parks and green spaces. Working under the direction of the Environmental Steward Crew Leaders and Natural Resources full-time staff, the Crew Member participates in a wide range of natural resource projects aimed at enhancing and maintaining the ecological health and biodiversity of county-owned lands. The Half-Time Environmental Steward Crew Member will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($12,752) paid equally over the course of 900 hours from the start to the end of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon completion ($3,697.50) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. These positions are half-time volunteers who will serve a minimum of 900 hours over 39 weeks, serving 30 hours per week. jobs.title: APAICS 2027 Summer Congressional Internship at Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies
jobs.description: Employer: Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies Expires: 12/01/2026 Program OverviewThe APAICS Summer Congressional Internship is a paid, eight-week program designed for undergraduate students and eligible recent graduates interested in gaining experience in public policy and public service. jobs.title: Cabin Counselor at Camp Bear Creek
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 12/01/2026 Cabin Counselor – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Being a Cabin Counselor is exhausting. It’s messy. It’s challenging. And it’s also one of the most rewarding things you can do with your summer.Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.What We’re Looking For:We want people who:Love working with kidsCan serve as strong, positive role modelsAre ready to lead Are excited to help young people grow in faithDon’t mind unplugging and spending a summer in the woodsWe aren't going to lie, being a camp counselor is incredibly hard work. You’ll be responsible for the daily care and well-being of the campers in your cabin — making sure they eat, sleep, brush their teeth, wear socks, and feel safe. It looks different each week and could mean sitting up with them at night when they're scared of the dark. It means teaching them how to paddle a kayak, supporting them at the rock wall/zip lines, building fires for skillet enchiladas (you’re going to love it), dancing to Grooveship worship and answering their questions about Jesus in Bible It also means picking up a kid when they fall in the dirt, giving them a high five when they finally hit the bullseye in archery, and letting them cover you in mud in the creek. It's all part of walking alongside campers through a week of fun, growth, and faith—and helping give them a summer they'll never forget.At Camp Bear Creek, counselors don’t just supervise- they lead. You’ll gain real world experience in:Leadership and public speakingCurriculum planning and facilitationConflict resolution and creative problem-solving Teamwork across diverse backgrounds. These soft skills are essential in every career field. You’ll also lead a variety of camp activities and work with different age groups- giving you the opportunity to grow into a well-rounded leader. We are also willing to work with you to ensure that this job can be used for internship credit in fields like Education, Public Health, Recreation & Leisure, Youth Services, Psychology and more. However, any student in any field can benefit from a summer camp experience like this. You’ll be part of an incredible team of about 30 college-aged staff from across Iowa, the U.S., and even around the world. We work hard. We play hard. We show up for each other every day. You’ll be surrounded by people who push you to grow — and who feel like family by the end of week one. This is more than a job. It’s a ministry, a leadership opportunity, and a summer you’ll never forget. You’ll give this job everything you’ve got — and it will give even more back.So, if you're looking for a summer full of purpose, adventure, community, and growth, don't let this opportunity pass you by. For more information about working at Camp Bear Creek or to apply, visit https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/

jobs.description: Employer: Reporters Without Borders Expires: 12/02/2026 Spring 2027 Internship - Reporters Without Borders USAReporters Without Borders/Reporters sans frontières (RSF), the world’s largest organization devoted to the safety, pluralism, and independence of journalism, is seeking an intern for its Washington, DC office (RSF USA) this fall. Communications:Oversee RSF USA’s internal press freedom newsletter by monitoring press freedom issues and sharing updates to RSF’s international staff on a daily basis.Help maintain a list of press contacts and make recommendations for press outreach opportunities. Support the drafting of press releases, social media posts, op-eds, and other written publications.Attend and/or contribute to the planning and execution of press freedom-related events. Fundraising:As needed, minimal assistance with:Building development pipelines through prospect and donor research.Donor record upkeep.Appeals/acquisitions via email and standard mail.Grant applications.Fundraising event support. LogisticsWe will consider applications for both full-time (40 hours per week) and part-time (minimum of 20 hours per week) interns for the spring term, which will start in January and conclude in May. The role operates in a hybrid office environment that requires two in-person work days a week for team collaboration and consistent use of office equipment such as computer, printer, and scanner. Thus, the intern must be residing in the Washington, DC area during the internship. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for internship opportunities at this time. In addition, the intern is paid a monthly stipend of $600 for part time and $1,000 for full time. Applicant Qualifications:Interested in press freedom, human rights, journalism and/or international nonprofits.Interested in the US policymaking process.Experience communicating with external stakeholders as part of an organization.Excellent communication (written and verbal).Developed research skills, including finding original sources, compiling data in impactful ways, and tailoring outputs for different audiences.Agility in task management, from long-term projects to breaking news responses.An eye for creative solutions to entrenched problems.Familiarity with using various software programs at other organizations.Strong time management.Media literate and an avid news consumer.Able to work in-person in Washington, DC during the summer per our hybrid (in-office/remote) schedule.Detail-oriented.Proactive.Reliable.Native-level English proficiency.French language skills not required, but a plus. jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/03/2026 Application Deadline12/18/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription*Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.EPA Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP), located in Durham, North Carolina.The mission of EPA is to protect human health and the environment. EPA works to ensure that: Americans have clean air, land and water; National efforts to reduce environmental risks are based on the best available scientific information; Federal laws protecting human health and the environment are administered and enforced fairly, effectively and as Congress intended; Environmental stewardship is integral to U.S. policies concerning natural resources, human health, economic growth, energy, transportation, agriculture, industry, and international trade, and these factors are similarly considered in establishing environmental policy; All parts of society have access to accurate information sufficient to effectively participate in managing human health and environmental risks; Contaminated lands and toxic sites are cleaned up; and chemicals in the marketplace are reviewed for safety.Research Project: The Risk Assessment Support Division (RASD) within the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s (US EPA) Office of Mission Critical Operations (OMCO) of the Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP) supports Agency decisions by providing solutions-driven research to rapidly evaluate the risks associated with environmental chemical exposures. A key component of this work is the application of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) including in vitro, in chemico, and in silico approaches to generate human relevant information for chemical hazard and risk assessment. These approaches support Agency's commitment to reduce or replace vertebrate animal testing while providing accurate and reliable data to safeguard human health and the environment. RASD develops and applies physiologically relevant in vitro models, high-throughput screening assays, and computational and informatics approaches to advance predictive, human-relevant toxicological assessment. As part of our in vitro NAM development, we are actively seeking a research participant to join our team and learn about the advancement of in vitro blood-brain barrier (BBB) models. You will gain experience with the establishment and optimization of in vitro BBB model systems, chemical exposure assays, and permeability and transport studies. Data generated through these studies will be used to inform in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation and support the development, parameterization, calibration, and evaluation of physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models of chemical disposition and brain exposure. The overall goal is to improve predictions of chemical brain exposure and distribution while advancing human-relevant approaches for chemical safety assessment. Learning Objectives: You will gain hands-on experience with human primary cell cultures, high-content imaging and image analysis, assessment of toxicokinetic assay endpoints, gene expression assays including qPCR and RNA sequencing, and advanced in vitro culture methods, such as 3D spheroids, organoids, and tissue chips. Additionally, you will be involved in curating scientific literature, preparing reports, presenting research at national meetings, and authoring manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals. Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Sreenivasa Ramaiahgari (ramaiahgari.sreenivasa@epa.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: December 14, 2026. All start dates are flexible and vary depending on numerous factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year and may be renewed three to four additional years upon EPA recommendation and subject to availability of funding.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.EPA Security Clearance: Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at EPA.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and EPA. Participants do not become employees of EPA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.ORISE offers all ORISE EPA graduate students and Postdocs a free 5 year membership to the National Postdoctoral Association (NPA).The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility.Questions: Please see the FAQ section of our website. If you have additional questions about the application process please email ORISE.EPA.OCSPP@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received or be currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in one of the relevant fields (biology, cell/molecular biology, biochemistry, toxicology, environmental science, or a closely related field of study). Preferred skills:Experience with in vitro cell culture and assay developmentFamiliarity with high-content imaging systems (epifluorescence or confocal microscopy)Experience with immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistryProficiency in molecular biology techniques, including DNA/RNA extractionsKnowledge of basic statistical methodsSkill in communicating scientific research through posters and oral presentationsExperience with, or courses in, open-source programming languages (R, Python)Highly self-motivated, well-organized, and innovative, with ability to act independently and collaborativelyStipend$52,693.00 – $64,453.00 YearlyPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsCitizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree.

EPA performs research to identify and validate alternative testing strategies that reduce reliance on costly and time-intensive animal studies while improving the speed and throughput of chemical hazard assessment. There are tens of thousands of chemicals currently in commerce, and only a small fraction have been assessed for developmental neurotoxicity. The DNT in vitro battery offers a path forward by combining complementary cell-based assays that capture key neurodevelopmental processes, including neuronal proliferation, migration, synaptogenesis, and network activity, into a tiered, mechanistically-informed testing framework. Building confidence in this battery requires rigorous assay development, robust data analysis, cross-agency collaboration, and linkage of in vitro endpoints to apical outcomes and regulatory points of departure. The objective of this research project is to advance the scientific credibility and regulatory utility of the DNT in vitro battery through integrated wet lab and bioinformatic approaches. You will contribute to assay development and optimization, perform comparative analyses of new and historical datasets, evaluate assay transferability across partner agencies, and conduct predictive analyses linking in vitro endpoints to apical toxicological outcomes. Under the guidance of a mentor, you will synthesize findings for peer-reviewed publication and stakeholder communication. jobs.title: EPA Internship: Analytical Chemist to Support New Approach Methodology and Endocrine Disruption at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/03/2026 Application Deadline12/18/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription*Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.EPA Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), located in Durham, North Carolina. The mission of EPA is to protect human health and the environment. EPA works to ensure that: Americans have clean air, land and water; National efforts to reduce environmental risks are based on the best available scientific information; Federal laws protecting human health and the environment are administered and enforced fairly, effectively and as Congress intended; Environmental stewardship is integral to U.S. policies concerning natural resources, human health, economic growth, energy, transportation, agriculture, industry, and international trade, and these factors are similarly considered in establishing environmental policy; All parts of society have access to accurate information sufficient to effectively participate in managing human health and environmental risks; Contaminated lands and toxic sites are cleaned up; and chemicals in the marketplace are reviewed for safety.Research Project: With thousands of commercial chemicals entering the environment, traditional animal-reliant safety assessments can no longer keep pace with the demand for rapid hazard and exposure data. To bridge this gap, EPA’s Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention is pioneering in vitro 'New Approach Method' (NAM) testing strategies to enable fast, cost-effective screening, prioritization, and human health risk assessments. This specific internship is deeply anchored within the analytical chemistry foundation necessary to validate and drive these alternative strategies forward.As an intern on our team, you will gain experience with EPA’s Risk Assessment Support Division by learning about analytical chemistry method development, validation, and execution. Your primary learning objective will be designing robust sample preparation and quantitative analysis procedures to track chemical concentrations and stability within complex in vitro and biochemical assay matrices, specifically targeted at biological perturbations such as endocrine disruption.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will learn to operate and troubleshoot advanced instrumentation, utilizing high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) and liquid/gas chromatography (LC-MS/MS, GC-MS/MS) to generate high-quality, reproducible kinetic profiles. By pairing your rigorous analytical measurements with exposure-dose and toxicokinetic modeling, you will directly enable the team to translate laboratory data into 'equivalent doses,' allowing scientists to compare systemic configurations against anticipated exposure levels to evaluate overall risk (hazard + exposure = risk).Learning objectives include:Advanced Method Development & Validation: Gain hands-on experience in designing, optimizing, and validating highly sensitive, selective analytical chemistry methods to extract and quantify trace-level organic chemicals across diverse and challenging biological and cell-culture matrices.High-Throughput Analytical Instrumentation: Master the operation, calibration, and troubleshooting of advanced instrumentation, including ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple-quadrupole and high-resolution mass spectrometers (UHPLC-MS/MS, Q-TOF).In Vitro Toxicokinetics (IVTK) Characterization: Develop proficiency in calculating chemical parameters, including hepatic metabolic clearance rates, plasma/media protein binding, and chemical stability, which are vital for determining points of departure for endocrine disruption pathways.Data Analysis Automation & Quality Assurance: Learn to implement automated data processing pipelines for mass spectrometry datasets, apply rigorous QA/QC metrics, and maintain strict data integrity practices matching good laboratory practices (GLP).Regulatory Integration & Cross-Disciplinary Teamwork: Understand how raw analytical chemistry data directly translates through exposure models to shape EPA screening, prioritization, and toxicological policy decisions, while enhancing collaborative communication across chemical and biological domains.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Deon Moore (moore.deon@epa.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: December 8, 2026. All start dates are flexible and vary depending on numerous factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year and may be renewed three to four additional years upon EPA recommendation and subject to availability of funding.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.EPA Security Clearance: Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at EPA.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and EPA. Participants do not become employees of EPA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.ORISE offers all ORISE EPA graduate students and Postdocs a free 5-year membership to the National Postdoctoral Association (NPA).The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility.Questions: Please see the FAQ section of our website. If you have additional questions about the application process, please email ORISE.EPA.OCSPP@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received or be currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in one of the relevant fields (chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or a related field, with an emphasis in analytical chemistry). Preferred skills:Demonstrated knowledge of laboratory operations, safety protocols, and quality practicesExperience with automated sample preparation systems, solvent evaporation units, homogenizers, centrifuges, HPLC, GC, mass spectrometry, and wet chemistry techniquesProficiency with laboratory and office software, including Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), LIMS, electronic laboratory notebooks, and instrument control softwareStrong technical writing skills, including preparation of detailed method documentation and maintenance of accurate laboratory recordsAbility to conduct literature searches using scientific databases and research toolsTraining or experience in organic chemistry, biochemistry, and analytical chemistry Stipend$52,693.00 – $64,453.00 YearlyPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsCitizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree.

jobs.description: Employer: National Institute of Standards and Technology Expires: 12/03/2026 The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) seeks undergraduate students for the Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) program. This vacancy announcement is for in-person fellowships in Gaithersburg, MD. An additional vacancy announcement is open for in-person fellowships in Boulder, CO (vacancy #SURF-2027-0002). Applicants may apply to both vacancies and use the same documents for all applications. Learn more at https://www.nist.gov/surf.Clarification from the agency:Current full-time undergraduate (first-year, sophomore, junior, or senior) degree-seeking students enrolled at accredited 2-year or 4-year colleges or universities in the U.S. or U.S. territories. Note: First-year and graduating seniors (defined as seniors participating in the Summer, Winter or Spring Commencement) are encouraged to apply to the program.Duties:The SURF program provides research opportunities for students to work with internationally known NIST scientists and engineers, to expose them to cutting-edge research and promote the pursuit of advanced degrees and careers in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). SURF gives students an opportunity to:Gain substantive career experience related to academic interestsAcquire lifelong leadership, management, and analytical skillsLearn about a career in public serviceBuild professional relationships, contacts, and networksObserve the daily operations and working environment of a premier federal laboratoryImagine Yourself in the NIST LaboratoriesNIST welcomes students from a broad range of STEM disciplines, including but not limited to biochemistry, biology, biophysics, chemistry, computer science, engineering, materials science, mathematics, nanoscale science, neutron research, physics, and statistics. Students work under the guidance of a research mentor in one of the participating laboratories or program offices. The following laboratories and offices participate in the SURF Gaithersburg program: Communications Technology Laboratory (CTL)Engineering Laboratory (EL)Information Technology Laboratory (ITL)Material Measurement Laboratory (MML) in partnership with the NIST Center for Neutron Research (NCNR)Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML)Other offices occasionally host SURF participants: Office of Advanced Manufacturing (OAM), Communications and Outreach Office (COO), Research Data and Computing Office (RDCO), Technology Partnerships Office (TPO), Standards Coordination Office (SCO)As part of the application process, all applicants must identify and select first and second-choice host laboratories/offices for placement consideration. For example, a computer science student may find project opportunities in CTL, PML, and EL in addition to the logical choice of ITL. Similar opportunities exist for those in other disciplines. For a detailed description of SURF projects in each NIST laboratory and prior acceptance rates, students are encouraged to review laboratory descriptions and acceptance rates at https://www.nist.gov/surf/surf-gaithersburg/research-programs. jobs.description: Employer: National Institute of Standards and Technology Expires: 12/03/2026 The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) seeks undergraduate students for the Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) program. This vacancy announcement is for in-person fellowships in Boulder, CO. An additional vacancy announcement is open for in-person fellowships in Gaithersburg, MD (vacancy #SURF-2027-0001). Applicants may apply to both vacancies and use the same documents for all applications. Learn more at https://www.nist.gov/surf.Clarification from the agency:Current full-time undergraduate (first-year, sophomore, junior, or senior) degree-seeking students enrolled at accredited 2-year or 4-year colleges or universities in the U.S. or U.S. territories. Note: First-year and graduating seniors (defined as seniors participating in the Summer, Winter or Spring Commencement) are encouraged to apply to the program.Duties:The SURF program provides research opportunities for students to work with internationally known NIST scientists and engineers, to expose them to cutting-edge research and promote the pursuit of advanced degrees and careers in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). SURF gives students an opportunity to:Gain substantive career experience related to academic interestsAcquire lifelong leadership, management, and analytical skillsLearn about a career in public serviceBuild professional relationships, contacts, and networksObserve the daily operations and working environment of a premier federal laboratoryImagine Yourself in the NIST LaboratoriesNIST welcomes students from a broad range of STEM disciplines, including but not limited to biochemistry, biology, biophysics, chemistry, computer science, engineering, materials science, mathematics, nanoscale science, neutron research, physics, and statistics. Students work under the guidance of a research mentor in in one of the participating laboratories. The following laboratories participate in the SURF Boulder program: Communications Technology Laboratory (CTL)Information Technology Laboratory (ITL)Material Measurement Laboratory (MML)Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML)As part of the application process, all applicants must identify and select first through fourth choice projects for placement consideration. Applicants should carefully choose projects because the completed application is considered primarily for first through third choice projects. Due to the multidisciplinary nature of NIST's research, we encourage students to look through the different laboratory websites to discover interesting project areas. For example, a computer science student may find project opportunities in CTL, PML, and MML in addition to the logical choice of ITL. Similar opportunities exist for those in other disciplines. For a detailed description of SURF projects in each NIST laboratory and prior acceptance rates, students are encouraged to review laboratory descriptions and acceptance rates at https://www.nist.gov/iaao/surf-program-research-opportunities-boulder-colorado. All students must work at the NIST campus in Boulder, CO for the entire appointment. While duties and responsibilities may vary by laboratory, all students must:Attend OrientationWork with their mentor on a designated research projectAttend the SURF seminar seriesCompose and submit an abstract halfway through the program summarizing research accomplishmentsDeliver an oral presentation during the final week of the program
