jobs.title: Career Advance Internship at San Francisco International Airport
jobs.description: Employer: San Francisco International Airport - San Francisco International Airport Expires: 12/03/2026 Are you a motivated student or recent graduate looking to gain hands-on experience while working at one of the nation’s leading airports? SFO’s Career Advance Internships provide motivated individuals with an opportunity to gain valuable hands-on work experience, develop professional skills, and contribute to the day-to-day operations and initiatives of San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Interns are placed in one of several Airport offices and paired with an SFO mentor who provides guidance, support, and opportunities for professional growth through daily assignments and larger-scale projects. In addition to their host office experience, interns receive ongoing support from SFO’s Career Pathways Team and participate in professional development opportunities, including airport tours, networking opportunities with Airport leadership, workshops, and other activities designed to broaden their understanding of airport operations, strengthen their skills, and prepare them for future career opportunities. Below is the list of host offices participating:1. Airport Director’s Office: The Director's Office Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in administrative operations and executive-level support while developing skills in communication, organization, research, writing, and document management. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will contribute to front desk operations, administrative projects, correspondence, and day-to-day office activities while gaining exposure to executive leadership and organizational processes.2. Airfield Safety: The Airfield Safety Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in aviation safety, training program evaluation, and data analysis while supporting efforts to enhance SFO's Airport Movement Area Training Programs and reduce runway incursions. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will work alongside airport safety and training professionals to evaluate initial, recurrent, and specialized driver training programs, identify knowledge gaps, and explore opportunities for improvement. The intern will assist with researching Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) guidance, industry best practices, emerging training technologies, and training approaches used at other airports. The intern will also support the review and analysis of training records, operational incidents, and deviation data to identify trends and develop recommendations for improving training effectiveness and knowledge retention. Through these assignments, the intern will develop skills in research, data analysis, interviewing, technical writing, and program evaluation while gaining an understanding of aviation human factors, airfield safety principles, and continuous safety improvement.3. Aviation Security and Regulatory Compliance: The Aviation Security (AVSEC) Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in airport security operations and regulatory compliance while developing an understanding of the policies, procedures, and technologies that support a safe and secure airport environment. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will work alongside AVSEC professionals to support the analysis, investigation, and resolution of operational incidents, as well as the planning of airport construction projects within restricted and public areas. The intern will also gain exposure to security infrastructure by participating in the inspection and testing of access control and closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems while developing skills in research, problem-solving, documentation, and regulatory compliance.4. Career Pathways: The Career Pathways Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in workforce development, program coordination, and project management while supporting SFO's Career Pathways programs. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will assist with coordinating internship and fellowship activities, supporting participant onboarding and engagement, organizing professional development workshops and airport tours, and communicating with interns, mentors, host offices, and community partners.The intern will also support program administration by maintaining tracking systems, organizing documentation, collecting participant feedback, and preparing reports and presentations. Through short- and long-term projects, the intern will gain exposure to program evaluation, data management, process improvement, and stakeholder engagement while contributing to SFO's efforts to develop a skilled future aviation workforce.5.Facilities (Scheduling and Control): The Facilities Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in facilities operations, asset management, preventive maintenance planning, and process improvement while supporting the Airport's Enterprise Facilities Management (EFM) initiative and implementation of IBM Maximo. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will work alongside the Scheduling & Control Unit, maintenance planners, engineers, and skilled trades personnel to assist with collecting and validating asset information, maintaining equipment inventories, and supporting preventive maintenance and inspection programs. The intern will also gain exposure to digital inspection tools, maintenance planning systems, and data reporting by assisting with the development of inspection checklists, maintenance job plans, reports, and dashboards. Through these assignments, the intern will develop skills in data management, research, documentation, project coordination, and process improvement while gaining an understanding of how facilities management supports safe, efficient, and reliable airport operations.6. IT Digital Transformation: The IT Digital Transformation Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in business analysis, project management, change management, enterprise asset management, digital transformation, business process improvement, and data analytics while supporting SFO's implementation of IBM Maximo as part of the Airport's broader Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) initiative.Working alongside IT professionals, project teams, and business stakeholders, the intern will assist with gathering, analyzing, and documenting business requirements; supporting project planning and coordination activities; identifying operational gaps and opportunities for process improvement; and analyzing and visualizing data to support informed decision-making. The intern will also gain exposure to enterprise systems, system integrations, asset governance, organizational change management, and project delivery practices while contributing to efforts that improve data quality, streamline business processes, facilitate user adoption, and strengthen asset management capabilities across the Airport.This internship provides valuable experience in business analysis, project management, change management, stakeholder engagement, data analytics, and enterprise technology while supporting initiatives that drive operational excellence and digital innovation.7. Reprographics: The Reprographics Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in graphic design, print production, and administrative operations while supporting San Francisco International Airport's (SFO) reprographics services. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will assist with developing and editing graphic design materials, preparing digital files for printing, and supporting the production of printed materials for various Airport divisions and initiatives.Working alongside reprographics professionals, the intern will gain exposure to the design and print production process, including project planning, layout and formatting, printing techniques, quality control, and coordination of print requests. The intern will also support day-to-day administrative activities, including organizing project files, maintaining records, tracking work requests, and assisting with general office coordination.Through short- and long-term projects, the intern will develop skills in visual communication, graphic design, print production, customer service, project coordination, and administrative support while contributing to SFO's internal communications and operational needs.8. Bureau of Planning & Environmental Affairs: The Planning and Environmental Affairs Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in airport planning and environmental affairs sections through guided learning and practical assignments.Environmental Affairs sectionThe Career Advance Intern will assist with regulatory compliance and reporting, natural resources management, and project coordination while supporting Airport maintenance and capital improvement projects. The intern will assist with gathering and analyzing environmental data, preparing documentation for federal and state environmental reviews, and supporting resource permit applications and regulatory submittals.The intern will also support implementation of SFO’s San Francisco Garter Snake (SFGS) Recovery Action Plan, including coordination and preparation of the calendar year 2027 work plan, project scheduling, environmental monitoring, documentation, and reporting in accordance with applicable permit requirements. Responsibilities will include supporting pre- and post-construction activities, participating in weekly project coordination meetings, and assisting with internal and external stakeholder engagement to inform the development of the next 10-year SFGS Recovery Action Plan.Airport Planning sectionThe Career Advance Intern will support a variety of airport planning studies and strategic initiatives by conducting research, data analysis, and documentation activities. The intern will assist with analyzing airport operational trends, passenger and facility data, and other planning metrics to help evaluate existing conditions and support future airport development efforts. Responsibilities may include preparing reports, presentations, maps, graphics, and other planning materials used to communicate findings and recommendations.Through these assignments, the intern will gain exposure to airport master planning, facilities planning, aviation forecasting, transportation planning, stakeholder coordination, and capital development processes while working closely with Airport Planning staff on projects that support the airport's long-term operational, infrastructure, and sustainability goals.9. Procurement Services: The Procurement Services Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in public-sector procurement, contract administration, training coordination, and departmental operations while developing skills in communication, organization, data management, and project coordination .Under the guidance of Procurement Services staff, the intern will assist with coordinating training sessions and procurement meetings, including scheduling, room reservations, vendor and participant communications, and preparation of training materials. Responsibilities will also include maintaining training records, and supporting related administrative activities.The intern will gain exposure to procurement and contract administration by assisting with organizing contract documentation, tracking contracts and task orders, supporting small-dollar purchasing activities, maintaining vendor databases, and coordinating vendor outreach. Additional assignments may include maintaining departmental databases and tracking tools, compiling information for reports, organizing electronic records, and preparing procurement-related documents and correspondence.More detailed information on the Career Advance internship can be found here: Career Advance Program 2027 | San Francisco International Airport Internship Details:Schedule: 24-32 hours per week in-person, Monday-Friday between 8:00 a.m. -5:00 p.m.Duration: 12 months How to QualifyEducation:1. Possession of a high school diploma; AND2.Completion of at least 90 semester units or 135 quarter units from an accredited college or university by the appointment date.***Please attach a copy of your unofficial transcript when submitting your applicationApplicants must meet the minimum qualification by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

jobs.title: 2027 PAID SUMMER LEGAL INTERNSHIPS at Legal Services of the Hudson Valley
jobs.description: Employer: Legal Services of the Hudson Valley Expires: 12/04/2026 About Us For more than 50 years, Legal Services of the Hudson Valley (LSHV) has been providing free, high-quality legal counsel in civil matters when basic human needs are at stake, including eviction and foreclosure prevention, domestic violence, disability, elder law, healthcare, consumer fraud and more. Our services support almost 600,000 poor and low-income families and individuals who cannot afford an attorney in our seven-county service area. With the gap separating those who can and cannot afford legal representation widening each day, we work to ensure that everyone has equal access to justice, regardless of their ability to pay. As the only provider of comprehensive civil legal services in the lower and mid-Hudson Valley (Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess, Rockland, Orange, Ulster and Sullivan), LSHV is proud to have handled over 12,000 cases impacting over 27,000 household members including over 10,000 children last year. LSHV is made up of ten offices, and a dedicated and highly skilled staff of attorneys, paralegals, and administrative professionals. Legal Services of Hudson Valley is dedicated to building a highly skilled workforce that reflects the diverse communities we serve and where everyone feels supported to bring their authentic selves to work. We are committed to racial justice and promoting equity for all, and we continuously review and strengthen our processes and practices to support our staff, clients and the communities we serve. Respect is a cornerstone of relationships among our staff. Our employee resource groups are self-directed and provide a space for members to support one another and their shared vision. We encourage applications from people of all identities and backgrounds. Fellowship Description LSHV will host 10 law student fellows in our housing units and 10 law student fellows in our general and/or other practice area units. Through these fellowships, LSHV will train the next generation of social justice lawyers, giving them both practical litigation experience and an understanding of the factors that create disadvantages for low-income individuals and families. While helping LSHV attorneys and staff serve clients, law fellows will receive training, mentorship, support, and skill development and engage in advocacy. Work may include client interviewing, issue spotting, legal research and writing, preparing court documents, accompanying attorneys and clients to court, and appearing in court under a student practice order. Housing Unit Fellows will help our clients to maintain the basic human and legal right to live in habitable housing and lend support to LSHV’s efforts to challenge landlord intimidation and harassment. General Practice Fellows will assist our staff attorneys in a variety of practice areas, including family law and domestic violence, housing, veterans’ benefits, public benefits, consumer debt, disability, and/or immigration law. Details 10-weekfellowship duration; 35 hours per work week required (5-day week, Mon – Fri) $8,000 stipend with 5 days paid time off (PTO) Fellows will be placed in LSHV offices throughout our service area, including White Plains, Yonkers, Mount Vernon, Peekskill, Poughkeepsie, New Windsor, Goshen, Nanuet, Monticello, and Kingston. Fellows will be loaned laptops during the summer for conducting LSHV business. Housing, transportation, work-related, and other fellowship expenses will be the law student's responsibility. LSHV will provide office parking where applicable. At the conclusion of the summer, fellows may be required to provide feedback concerning their experience, the substance of which may be reproduced in full or in part in LSHV materials. Eligibility Open to law students enrolled in a U.S. law school who will have completed two years of law school by May 2027 or are graduating in 2027. Must not have previously accepted an LSHV Paid Summer Legal Fellowship (previously titled LSHV Paid Summer Legal Internship). Must be able to work several days per week in person in the office where placed (our offices are hybrid, subject to disability-related reasonable accommodations. Ability to travel to the office where placed and other locations, such as courts, as needed. Application Timeline All materials must be submitted by Monday, December 21, 2026, at 11:59 pm (ET) Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered. Applicants selected for interviews will be notified in early January 2027. Finalists will be notified in early February 2027. Required Submissions Applications will be evaluated based upon review of the following: Complete Online Application with preferred office locations and practice areas Unofficial Law School Transcript Current Resume One legal writing sample on any topic (5-page limit) Statement of Interest (typed, double-spaced) Describe your commitment to public interest law and/or direct legal services, and what you hope to gain from LSHV’s Summer Internship Program. Please explain why you are interested in the practice area(s) you have preference in your application. You may include information such as personal experience, prior jobs, volunteer experience or internships and what you learned from them, as well as future career plans and professional goals. (750-word max) Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please email us at accommodate@lshv.org or call 914-949-1305 This email is created exclusively to assist disabled job seekers whose disability prevents them from being able to apply online. Only messages left for this purpose will be returned.

jobs.title: Winter Internship at Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, AFL-CIO
jobs.description: Employer: Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, AFL-CIO Expires: 12/04/2026 Who we are:HTC is the union for hotel and gaming workers in New York and New Jersey. We are widely recognized as the most powerful union in this industry in the world, with the best contracts. Our largely immigrant membership enjoys a middle class lifestyle, free family healthcare, the ability to retire with a pension. The children of our members have the opportunity to go to college and become professionals because of their parents’ hard work. This is unheard of in an industry where workers are generally exploited and living in poverty.Unlike most unions, our membership is expanding, and in the last ten years our membership has grown from 25,000 to over 40,000. In state and local politics, we are famous for “punching above our weight.” That’s because our membership loves their union and actively volunteers more than most union members.If you want to fight for social justice and win, this is the best place to do it.This role:The Winter Internship will take place from Monday, January 4th – Friday, January 22nd at our office in Midtown, Manhattan. During this 3-week internship, interns will gain hands-on exposure to different departments and roles within the organization. Interns will attend in-person grievance meetings and sit in on union-management negotiations with our contract enforcement team. Interns will also go into the field with our member mobilization team, traveling from shop to shop to communicate with members about pressing issues and mobilize them to upcoming union events. Interns will also work closely with the communications department, writing articles to report on union victories and events and working on other media projects requiring creativity and persuasiveness.This position is ideal for students with a passion for social justice, strong writing abilities, and the desire to learn.Qualifications:Demonstrated commitment to social justice;Ability to communicate respectfully and comfortably with people from diverse backgrounds;Ability to write persuasively, clearly, and creatively;Desire and ability to learn quickly and grow into positions of greater responsibility;Thorough attention to details;Ability to multitask, work efficiently, be well organized and reliable;Resourcefulness and talent for problem-solving;Persistence and determination;Loyalty to the organization, with a sense of integrity.Extra consideration will be given for ANY of the following qualifications:Bilingual (in addition to English), especially in Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, Vietnamese, Russian, Polish or Bengali;Strong computer skills and the ability to quickly learn new computer programs;Talent for photography, videography, and/or media design;Experience working in the hotel, restaurant, hospitality, or other service industries.Hours:35 hours/weekPay:$20Location:Midtown, Manhattan (in-person)How to Apply:In addition to a resume and references, applicants must include a cover letter. The cover letter should be clear and concise and explain which position you are applying for, the specific reasons for your interest in the position, and specify (with appropriate explanation) which of each of the listed qualifications you possess and which ones you do not possess. The cover letter, resume, and references should be emailed to: careers@nyhtc.org, with the subject line “Winter Internship #INT#”.The Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, AFL-CIO, is an equal opportunity employer. All persons regardless of age, race, ethnicity, gender, religious affiliation and sexual orientation are encouraged to apply.
